My hair is curly and I cut it (just cut it this very morning, actually!). Here are the tricks I've learned:

1. Cut it DRY.

2. Pull it taught, all the way straight, then lift it up a few inches depending on how curly your curls are (for me I lift around 4 inches)

3. Cut LONGER than you think you want. If you think you want to take off 3 inches, take off 2 instead.

Your hair will gain some curl by losing the weight, so it will wind up shorter than you expect. Cutting it dry allows you to see the natural curl patterns as they are, which helps to keep the dreaded triangle of doom appearing on your head, and keeps the cuts consistent. Every time I went to someone my hair would be a jacked up mess because they cut it wet, pulled it tight, and then cut. It was never even remotely even, and always took a few weeks of regrowth to not be horrific.

I have started asking my usual hairdresser to cut my hair dry for this reason. The curls on top are tighter than the waves underneath, and so the ends were never evenly layered once it dried. But if it's cut dry, it works perfectly.
